claims.verbatim:
Ship Harpswell, Owen, Havre, April 1, with mdse and 125[?]
passengers, to Boyd & Hincken. Was 6 days in the Channel;
had heavy westerly gales most of the passage; had 2 deaths.
April 15, lat 46 06, lon 22 50, while lying too in a heavy SW
gale, was boarded by a sea, carrying away part of fore chan-
nels, main rail and bulwarks, flooding the decks and between
decks. (See Marine Disasters.)

claims.verbatim:
Brig Fred H Parker—Ship Harpswell, Capt Owen, from
Havre, which arrived at this port yesterday, reports April
17, lat 47 08, lon 24 04, was spoken by brig Thetis (Br), from
Alvarado for Liverpool, having on board Capt McNeely and
crew of brig Fred H Parker (Br), who were taken off that
vessel April 3, and wished to be transferred to the H, as they
were short of provisions and the vessel was leaking; took
them on board and brought them to this port. Capt Mc-
Neely reports:—Sailed from St John, NB, March 20 for Porto
Rico, with a cargo of lumber, and had heavy weather; on
27th, while lying too under three-reefed mainsail, in a heavy
gale from NW, his vessel capsized, when the masts were cut
away, and she righted, losing everything off deck and one of
the crew; vessel full of water; was without food, except
some flour and saltish water, for seven days, when, on April
3, were taken off by the Thetis. [The F H Parker was ten
months old, of 132 tons burthen, was owned by Capt McNeely
and others, and insured at Cornwallis, NS, for $3000.] The
Thetis needed no assistance from the Harpswell.
